articles.title: TRY GOOGLE PICS: EASY IMAGE CREATION AND EDITING IN GOOGLE WORKSPACE
articles.summary: Google Pics, an image creation and editing tool built on the Nano Banana model, reaches Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and most Workspace business customers. Object segmentation, in-image text editing and translation, and collaborative editing give precise control over an image rather than regenerating it from scratch. Integration is available in Docs and Slides, with Drive arriving in the coming weeks.

articles.title: UPDATES TO GENERATIVE PLUGINS AND SHADERS
articles.summary: Custom generative plugins and shaders, built by prompting the Figma agent, gain animated and interactive shaders that respond to motion and mouse input. Creations can now be published to the Community or to an organization, and a code viewer exposes the underlying shader and plugin code. MCP updates let third-party agents modify plugins and shaders, with shaders rendering correctly in generated React code.

articles.title: LEAKERS BATTLE OVER WHETHER THIRD IPHONE 18 PRO COLOR WILL BE SILVER OR BLACK
articles.summary: Leaks continue to point to Dark Cherry/Burgundy and Sky Blue as two of the iPhone 18 Pro's launch colors. The main uncertainty is the third finish, with some well-known leakers claiming Apple will offer black while others believe silver is more likely. Until Apple's announcement next week, both options remain plausible, though recent reports suggest silver and black are the final contenders.

articles.title: ECOSYSTEM DESIGN
articles.summary: Ecosystem design pushes past the product boundary, shaping the conditions and capabilities people need to succeed on a platform rather than the interface itself. Integrations, partnerships, marketplaces, developer platforms, community development, and corporate development are the six surfaces where a product becomes a world other people build on. Five practices follow: design the whole customer loop, treat third parties as users with business models, build trust, tend community, and treat docs as a product.

articles.title: IS PRODUCT DISCOVERY A PHASE OR A WEEKLY HABIT?
articles.summary: Product discovery works as weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, not as a kickoff phase that hands a backlog to engineering. Discovery and delivery are two kinds of work on one team, and a high kill rate is the test that discovery is real. Recruiting is the bottleneck: a Monday-to-Friday cadence survives only when a conversation is already on the calendar, even a customer-support ride-along.

articles.title: AI IS MAKING PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT FASTER. BUT WHERE DID THE WORK GO?
articles.summary: AI can dramatically speed up individual tasks like research synthesis, prototyping, and code generation, but that doesn't automatically make the entire product development process faster. Often the work doesn't disappear—it shifts into review, verification, refactoring, or downstream teams, creating hidden costs that can erode the initial gains. The real question isn't whether AI increases local productivity, but whether it improves the whole system's ability to turn ideas into reliable products without accumulating technical debt, instability, or rework.

articles.title: ON ANIMATING WHAT YOU CAN'T SEE
articles.summary: A ghosted double image in DuckDuckGo for iOS's floating toolbar survived three rounds of retiming because the bug was view ownership, not animation timing. Recording the transition at 60fps and stepping through it with ffmpeg showed the tab-count badge fully visible 24 frames before the snapshot animation began. Two failure modes generalize: snapshotting a view's bounds instead of what it draws, and resizing a snapshot instead of scaling it.

articles.title: RENÉ BIEDER'S NEURATH X IS A GEOMETRIC TYPEFACE MADE FOR THE AGE OF AI
articles.summary: A new typeface family explores how far geometric reduction can be pushed without sacrificing readability, drawing inspiration from early modernist experiments in typography and visual communication. Built as both proportional and monospaced families with extensive stylistic alternates, it reimagines the unrealized radical potential of classics like Futura while balancing mathematical purity with practical usability. The release extends beyond the typeface itself through a coordinated visual identity of 3D animation, motion design, and sound, all expressing the same philosophy of clarity, reduction, and geometric transformation.

articles.title: THE NEW DISNEY WORLD LOGO DESIGN IS ACTUALLY KIND OF GENIUS
articles.summary: Disney World's upcoming 55th-anniversary logo is earning praise for cleverly combining two “5”s into unmistakable Mickey Mouse ears while reviving elements of the resort's original 1971 globe logo. Fans have responded far more positively than they did to the 50th-anniversary mark, praising its simplicity, nostalgia, and stronger visual concept.
